lens: Brand and product guardian — PRODUCT.md ("night, minimal, focused"; flow over menus; the board is sacred; one violet accent; no pressure, no timers) and DESIGN.md (calm and airy, generous whitespace, the game screen is nothing but arrows, hearts and floating circular buttons) read in full, checked against the code the plan cites.

kills.reason: Visual combo escalation is the hyper-casual reward grammar the brand is defined against. PRODUCT.md's user model is explicit — 'short relaxed sessions... no timers, no pressure' — and a bead that thickens on your 8th tap inside a 1200 ms window is a speed reward, i.e. a timer with the numbers hidden. DESIGN.md scopes in-game motion to 'feedback and flow'; bead width on tap N carries no information about the board. It is also the most expensive cheap step in W2: it moves combo computation out of GameScreen into BoardView.handleTap and changes onRemoved's signature, i.e. a refactor of the single hottest code path in the app, to ship a feature that is flagged OFF by default. The step's own FLAGCHECK concedes 'escalation itself is on the anti-reference list' and then builds it anyway.
kills.replacement: Do not build it. Instead spend the step asking the inverse question the plan never asks: EXIT_COMBO_ESCALATES already ships audio pitch escalation today. Put ONE recording of an eight-tap burst with pitch escalation ON and OFF in front of the owner and let them decide whether the existing audio combo should be REMOVED. That is the same evidence artifact, zero code risk, and it tests the brand question in the direction the brand actually points.

kills.reason: It ships PRESS_PREVIEW_RAMP_MS defaulted to 0, i.e. today's exact behaviour, and then demands the single most expensive verification in the entire plan (a paired A/B/A across an alternating emulator session with sample-count reconciliation) to prove the no-op is a no-op. The decision it reopens was already settled by measurement: docs/perf-tap-forgiveness-ab-2026-09-08.md records that drawing the preview at touch-down cost enough to warrant the 64 ms PRESS_PREVIEW_DELAY_MS gate, and both renderers carry an explicit comment saying the snap is deliberate. Reopening a measured decision to ship it off-by-default is ceremony, and it is ranked last in its own workstream by its own author.
kills.replacement: Delete the step. If the snap ever reads wrong on a real device, reopen it then with the device in hand — not now, on an emulator whose host load has already made absolute gates unevaluable once.

kills.reason: This is the plan's largest brand inversion and it is never named as one. DESIGN.md: 'no board frame, no grid lines, no tile backgrounds, no header divider — the game screen is nothing but the arrows, the hearts and three floating circular buttons', plus 'Calm and airy' and 'Generous whitespace'. The audit reframed that airiness as a defect ('huge dead space top and bottom', 'dead vertical bands') and W5-07 acts on the reframing without ever putting it to the owner. It puts chrome INSIDE BoardView's viewport — the one region both documents fence off. Second problem: it collides with W5-05. W5-05 puts the silhouette badge 'beside the level label in the GameScreen header'; W5-07's top band carries 'the W5-05 silhouette badge plus the level number'. Either the badge ships twice or W5-07 silently kills half of W5-05, and no step says which. Third: every ACCEPT criterion is geometric (no overlap at fit-to-view, opacity 0 after pinch, taps pass through). Not one asks whether the result looks better than the empty margin it fills — which is the only question that matters and the one this project's own rules say closes visual work.
kills.replacement: Do not implement until the owner has seen a same-level, same-zoom screenshot pair (bands vs today's empty margin) on the 360 dp geometry in both themes and said yes. Then constrain it hard: bands may only RELOCATE elements that already exist in the header, total on-screen element count on the game screen must not increase, and W5-05's header badge is deleted if the band carries it. If the owner says the empty margin is the brand, the step dies and W5-05's badge stays in the header — which is the cheaper, safer outcome.

kills.reason: The shields half is well-evidenced and should ship. The visibility half runs against both DESIGN.md and the plan's own research. DESIGN.md deliberately specifies 'streak/run parts shown only from 2 up' inside a single quiet ink-dim line; W4-06 promotes the streak to its own element directly under the daily entry and shows it from 1. Starting a loss-aversion counter on a player's first solve is exactly the pressure texture a 'no timers, no pressure, before bed' product is defined against — and the step cites JMIR 2023 (n=14,879) finding rigid daily temporal consistency predicted WORSE long-term persistence, then makes the daily cadence MORE prominent. It also adds a second token ('· 1 saved') to a menu that four other steps are already adding rows to.
kills.replacement: Ship the shields (forgiveness is the genuinely evidenced half — Duolingo's cap 1→2-3 result). Keep the streak in the existing lifetime-stats line, keep 'from 2 up', and delete the standing '· 1 saved' token. Surface forgiveness only at the moment it means something: when a shield is actually SPENT, show one transient line on the next menu open ('Your streak was saved'). That delivers the whole message without a permanent counter, and it needs no DESIGN.md edit.

kills.reason: An evening push notification is a pressure channel inserted into a product whose stated purpose is the absence of pressure, and the step's own sourced evidence argues against it on every axis: gaming is the worst-performing notification vertical at under 1% CTR, uninstall risk rises sharply in the 2-5/week band, and the JMIR study found evening use decayed fastest — which is the exact slot the escalation recommends (20:30). The engineering design is genuinely disciplined (never on a played day, dead after 3 unengaged days, no streak threat in the copy). That is not the problem. The problem is that it is sequenced in W4, ahead of W6, so there is no instrumentation capable of telling you whether a sub-1% channel earned its uninstall risk. You would be shipping an unmeasurable brand-cost feature.
kills.replacement: Hold until W6 telemetry is live, then gate on two owner answers: (1) does a calm before-bed product get to interrupt bedtime at all, and (2) will you actually kill it if the measured tap-through is under 1%? If the answer to (2) is not a committed yes with a named metric and a kill date, do not build it.

kills.reason: It spends a finite, non-renewable resource on an unmeasured guess. Apple caps prompts at 3 per 365 days; the step self-caps at 3 lifetime; the engagement gate N is set to 25 solves and the escalation states plainly 'It is not measured and I will not dress it as one.' That honesty is correct and is exactly why it should not ship yet: firing at the wrong N burns a prompt you cannot get back, and W6 (which could tell you the totalSolved distribution at which players are actually satisfied) is sequenced after W4. The gate logic itself is fine; the timing is not.
kills.replacement: Build the gate module and its tests now (it is pure and cheap), but ship with the trigger disabled. Enable it after W6 gives you a totalSolved distribution, and set N from the measured point where perfect-clear rate peaks — the same discipline W1-07 applies to FTUE_STALL_HINT_MS and W7-11 applies to ad pacing.

kills.reason: W0-01 and W7-03 are the same fix specified twice with different semantics. W0-01 gates on `__DEV__` alone; W7-03 gates on `__DEV__ || Platform.OS === 'web'`. Whichever lands second either weakens the other's guarantee or reverts it. W0-01's acceptance ('grep dist/ for TEST AD returns zero') is also incompatible with W7-03's web allowance if the web export is ever checked.
kills.replacement: Delete the fake-ad half of W7-03 and keep W0-01 as the single owner, with W7-03's web clause folded into it (`__DEV__ || Platform.OS === 'web'`). Same for W0-05 vs W7-03's initAds-retry half: one owner, W0-05, with W7-03's AppState-resume trigger folded in.

kills.reason: W7-11 rewrites the exact function W0-06 writes (showInterstitialIfDue / registerGameFinished), adds three more rules on top, and moves the decision into a new src/ui/adPolicy.ts. W0-06 also permanently adds `arrows_finished_games` to the frozen PersistenceKeys and to the exact-array assertion in storage.test.ts:36 — persisted schema, which this project's own rules say must not be churned. Shipping W0-06 means adding a persisted key and a counter implementation that a later workstream immediately replaces.
kills.replacement: Cut W0-06's persistence and pacing work; keep only its one genuinely urgent line — never zero the counter on a path where no ad displayed. Move the persisted key and the after-a-loss interstitial into W7-11, which is the step that actually owns ad pacing and has the baseline (W7-12) to justify the values.

kills.reason: W0-07 and W5-02 are the same contrast repair, done twice, by two workstreams, with two different failure counts (seven pairs vs six) and two different test files (src/ui/__tests__/theme.test.ts vs src/ui/__tests__/contrast.test.ts) and two different audit scripts. They also disagree on method: W0-07 reaches for shape (struck glyph, outlined pip) plus token tweaks; W5-02 adds a new `inkDisabled` role and raises `border`. Whichever lands second will find its own 'pre-fix failure' already fixed, invalidating its acceptance criterion, which in both cases is 'the script must exit non-zero on HEAD listing the failures'.
kills.replacement: One owner, one script, one test file. W5-02 is the better-specified of the two (it composites the actual panel scrims, which W0-07 misses entirely, and it bans shadow/elevation as the depth mechanism — the correct call for an ink-dark ground). Hoist W5-02 into W0 and delete W0-07, keeping only W0-07's shape-over-colour instinct (struck sound glyph, outlined spent pip) as W5-02 acceptance criteria.

kills.reason: W0-03 and W2-02 touch the identical six withTiming call sites (BoardView.tsx:842/887/934 and StaticBoardSurface.native.tsx:264/308/348) with two different specifications. W0-03 passes ReduceMotion.Never AND skips starting the driver AND threads a reducedMotion parameter into feedbackCurves; W2-02 passes ReduceMotion.Never and leaves the worklet branches in place. W2-02's acceptance is stated as a HEAD-vs-patched frame comparison ('on HEAD the same capture contains zero such frames') — which becomes false the moment W0-03 ships, so W2-02 arrives with an unreproducible pre-fix baseline, the exact condition this project's review rules say must lower confidence.
kills.replacement: W0-03 owns the three feedback-layer sites and the fallback rendering. Reduce W2-02 to what W0-03 does not cover: an explicit reduceMotion policy on the remaining ~21 call sites (splash, stars, heart pip, Play breathing, hint recentre) plus the jest source-scan that fails on any call site missing the key. Restate its acceptance against those sites, not against the three W0-03 already fixed.

kills.reason: Five workstreams independently append to the same Object.freeze'd PersistenceKeys array (verified: 8 entries today, saveSystem.ts:41-49) and each independently rewrites the same exact-array assertion at storage.test.ts:36-45. W0-06 says 9 keys, W1-03 says 9, W3-01 says 10, W6-03 says 9, W4-01 says 'exactly 19 entries' whose 'first eight are byte-identical to the current list' — a premise that is already false if W0-06, W1-03 or W3-01 has landed. Worse, W4-01 and W6-03 BOTH define a key named `arrows_schema_version` with different meanings (save-schema version vs telemetry-schema version). This is a guaranteed merge collision in the one subsystem this project's own rules single out for migration and wipe-risk scrutiny, and no step owns the reconciliation.
kills.replacement: Add a single step, before any of them, that lands the full final key list in one migration with one schema-version key, one owner, and one updated assertion — then have W0-06/W1-03/W3-01/W4-01/W6-03 consume keys that already exist rather than each extending the array. Assign `arrows_schema_version` to the save system only; telemetry keys live entirely under the `arrows_tel_` prefix outside PersistenceKeys, as W6-03 itself already argues.

kills.reason: Three workstreams each build a screen-capture harness over the same adb plumbing in scripts/perf/android/benchmark.mjs: W2-01 (capture-motion.mjs — screenrecord plus ffmpeg frame split, asserts animator scale is 1), W5-01 (capture-device.mjs — screencap without PERF_MODE, aborts if animator scale is 0), W6-13 (--record inside benchmark.mjs, plus assert-rendered). All three exist to solve the same two problems: PERF_MODE cannot reach splash/menu/panels, and the harness forces animator_duration_scale to 0. Building it three times triples the cost and guarantees three different manifests, three different frame rates and three incomparable artifact sets across the very workstreams whose acceptance depends on comparing frames.
kills.replacement: Build it once, first, as W2-01 (the most complete spec: manifest with git HEAD, serial, API level, read-back animator scale, and a demonstrated ability to photograph a 300 ms effect). W5-01 becomes 'add --screen and --theme to the existing capture tool'; W6-13 becomes 'add assert-rendered on top of it'. This also removes a real hazard: W5-01 and W2-01 currently disagree on whether the tool refuses to run at animator scale 0 or merely records the value.

kills.reason: The step's own measurement answers its own question and the plan does not act on the answer. It computes the fillet delta at 0.048 cell, which at the median fit-to-view cell (16.1 dp) is 0.77 dp against a 2.32 dp resting stroke, and 0.41 dp on the densest board — below perceptual threshold at the state DESIGN.md says every level opens in. Implementing it would require changing arrowGeometry.ts's path emission, the delimited text geometry protocol, and BOTH native parsers including the Swift renderer that has not compiled since 2026-09-01, and would raise per-arrow path command count on 200+ arrow boards. That is the highest-risk change in W5 for the least visible return.
kills.replacement: Collapse to a one-line documentation fix inside W5-02's DESIGN.md pass: 'bends are rounded by the stroke's own round join, outer radius 0.072 cell; the ~0.12 figure was never implemented.' Drop the six-PNG owner review entirely — the numbers already decided it. If the owner later wants crisp turns at high zoom, that is a separate brief written after iOS compiles.

kills.reason: The escalation recommends granting the free-mistakes assist on exactly ONE real level, and justifies it as measurement discipline: 'not because one is measured to be right, but because any larger number is an invented threshold.' That reasoning does not hold — 1 is precisely as invented as 3, and the argument is timidity wearing the costume of rigour. It also runs against the only evidence the plan cites on the question: Li et al. KDD 2021 puts too-hard at 0.160 churn hazard versus too-easy at 0.053 for players in their first ten days, i.e. the asymmetry says err generous. The audit's own repro was losing three hearts in six taps on level 1 with no rule ever stated.
kills.replacement: Either state honestly that 1 is a taste call and put it to the owner alongside 3 with the KDD asymmetry attached, or define the assist by condition rather than count: forgiveness stays on until the player clears a board without spending a heart, then ends permanently. That is a defensible rule derived from the thing being taught rather than a number pulled from the air, and it self-terminates for a competent player on level 1.

kills.reason: The step congratulates itself for expressing its memory gates as fractions of a measured baseline rather than as the inherited unsourced 16 MB / 20 MB figures — and then invents the fractions. 'At most 20% of the W8-03 baseline delta' and 'at most 25% of the W8-03 largest region' are picked numbers layered on top of a measurement that has not been taken yet. Nothing in W8-03 produces 20% or 25%; they are the same class of unmeasured threshold the plan correctly refuses elsewhere (W1-07, W2-09, W3-04, W7-11).
kills.replacement: State the gate qualitatively and let W8-03 supply the number: 'after the refactor, no CA/IOSurface/CG-raster region scaling with board dimensions appears in the VM Tracker snapshot.' That is the actual claim (the bitmap backing store is gone), it is falsifiable by inspection, and it does not require a fraction nobody measured. Same correction applies to W8-07's 'within 15%' repeatability bar and its 'within 5%' frame reconciliation.

unmeasured_numbers: W0-02 SPLASH_MAX_MS = 4000 ms — the 2630 ms animation completion is real, the 1370 ms of headroom on top of it is picked. Nothing measured says a cold splash cannot exceed 4 s on a slow device, and this is the timer that decides whether a player is stuck.
W0-05 initAds retry schedule '3 attempts at 5 s / 15 s / 45 s' — written with 'e.g.' in the brief, which is the tell. No measurement of real init-failure recovery times produced it.

W2-07 anticipation magnitude — the step requires the existing `d >= 0` assertion to be replaced by 'a bound on the negative excursion as a stated fraction of the peak' and never states the fraction. The implementer invents the number that decides whether the arrow visibly recoils or does nothing.

W3-08 poolSize ≈ 40 (26 existing + ~14 new silhouettes) — self-flagged as provisional, but it is the number that sets W3-06's entire acceptance table (per-shape share 200/poolSize, first-appearance ≤ poolSize) and it drives an L-sized art commission. Derived from '5-6 levels per session', itself unmeasured — this repo has no session telemetry.

W4-07 tile rasterization at 14 rows and the ~20 dp gallery tile size — picked. The step's own acceptance asks whether 26 silhouettes are 'recognisable' at that size, which is exactly the question the unmeasured number decides.

W4-08 share card ceilings: 12-column downsample, ≤240 characters, ≤16 grid rows — all picked. 12 columns is the number that determines whether a Cat still reads as a Cat after downsampling, and nothing measured it.
W4-09 notification hour 20:30 and the '3 consecutive days without opening' cutoff — both picked. The step's own evidence (evening use decays fastest) argues against the first.
W4-10 review-prompt engagement gate N = 25 lifetime solves — self-flagged as unmeasured, correctly, and then shipped anyway on a finite lifetime quota.

W5-05 silhouette badge at ~20 dp in the header and ~64 dp on the panel — picked. 20 dp is precisely the threshold at which the step's own blind-naming acceptance ('a third party can identify it as a cat') becomes doubtful.
W5-07 the 15 dp clearance margin in 'min slack >= band height + 15 dp' — the 111/126/146 dp slack figures are genuinely measured; the 15 dp buffer that turns them into a 96 dp band cap is not.
W8-04 memory gates at 20% of baseline delta and 25% of the largest region — invented fractions of a baseline W8-03 has not yet produced.
W8-07 harness repeatability bar 'two runs within 15%' and frame reconciliation 'to within 5%' — both picked, and they are the numbers that decide whether the iOS instrument is trusted at all.

W6-08 gamesPerInterstitial clamp upper bound of 10 — the step concedes the upper bound is a taste decision, which means a remote config value can legally set an ad every ten levels or every one, with nothing measured behind either end.
W1-08 / escalation 2: the first-run assist covers exactly 1 real level — presented as measurement discipline, but 1 is as unmeasured as 3.
sequencing_errors: W2 (12 steps of motion and feel) precedes W3 (the level-indexed difficulty curve). The plan's own research names difficulty as 'the best-evidenced retention lever' (KDD 2021, 14,615 vs 14,687 users, 10-day A/B) and its own measurements say difficulty is flat forever — level 1 = 60 arrows, level 1000 = 97, mean 96.2 over levels 1-30 versus 100.4 over levels 171-200. Polishing the exit slither and the panel entrance of a game that never gets harder is polishing the wrong surface. The two steps in W2 that carry actual teaching value — W2-05 (the 350 ms lose delay truncates the 650 ms blocker flash at 54% of its run, cutting off the game's only explanation of its core rule at the single most instructive moment) and W2-02's reduce-motion policy — should be hoisted next to W0-03; the rest should follow W3.

W6 (instrumentation) is sixth, behind W3 and W4. Every retention claim in W3 and W4 is unfalsifiable without it. W3-02's probe is explicit that it 'measures search cost, not human difficulty' and 'has never been correlated with a real player's mistake rate' because there is no analytics. W4 then ships a daily board, a streak, notifications and a store-review prompt — four retention systems, none of which can be evaluated, one of which (W4-10) spends a finite lifetime quota. W6-01/02/03/04 (schema, call sites, store, transport) belong immediately after W0.

W7-01/02 (EEA/UK consent) sits in the seventh workstream while the exposure is live right now: no CMP, no GDPR flow, no CCPA, no COPPA flag, `setConsent` never called anywhere in src/, and app.json already declares AD_ID. W7's own escalation concedes 'the existing ad exposure is unchanged by W6 and is already live' and that this is 'the pre-existing risk'. W0's stated goal is 'stop the bleeding' and it contains a fake-ad modal fix, a splash backstop and a contrast pass — none of which can get the listing removed. Consent, the privacy policy correction (W7-05) and the DSA trader declaration (W7-09) are the actual W0.

W4-05/06 depend on the W4-01 save migration, W1-03 depends on its own migration, W3-01 on its own, W6-03 on its own, W0-06 on its own — five migrations against one frozen 8-key array with one exact-array assertion. There is no ordering under which all five acceptance criteria ('exactly 9 keys' / 'exactly 10' / 'exactly 19 with the first eight byte-identical') are simultaneously true.

W5-05 (silhouette badge in the GameScreen header) and W5-07 (top overlay band carrying 'the W5-05 silhouette badge plus the level number') are sequenced adjacently and contradict each other. No step declares whether the badge is relocated or duplicated.

W0-03 must precede W1-06 and W1-07, and W1-07 says so explicitly ('this step is blocked on the reduce-motion fix and says so'), but W1-06's reduce-motion acceptance criterion does not carry the same dependency and would pass vacuously if run first. W2-02 then re-specifies the same fix a workstream later, arriving with a pre-fix baseline W0-03 has already destroyed.
missing_work: Nobody owns the composite HomeScreen. Today it holds 7 elements (2 header buttons, wordmark, 'Level N', difficulty label, Play pill, stats line). The plan adds a Settings header button (W7-04), a 'Today's board · done' row (W4-05), a promoted streak line with a shield token (W4-06) and a collection entry (W4-07) — roughly 11 elements. Every step individually passes its own brand gate by pleading 'quiet', 'inkDim', 'no second violet pill'. No step checks the total against DESIGN.md's 'generous whitespace' or PRODUCT.md's anti-reference 'cluttered... menus the player navigates every session'. Add a step that owns the finished menu composition and closes on an owner screenshot, before any of those four land.

Nobody owns the composite game-screen chrome either. Verified today: back button, 'LEVEL N', mission label, '{remaining} left', heart pips, hint button — already past DESIGN.md's 'nothing but the arrows, the hearts and three floating circular buttons'. The plan adds a silhouette badge (W5-05), two in-viewport overlay bands (W5-07), a transient 'Hint unavailable' line (W0-04) and tutorial copy (W1-05, W1-06). Same gap: per-step FLAGCHECKs all pass, the aggregate is never looked at.

No step rewrites PRODUCT.md. The plan measured its central product claim false — 'The puzzle is finding the order' (PRODUCT.md line 19) against 50 random-greedy playthroughs clearing in exactly arrowCount taps with zero dead ends, and a monotonicity proof that no order can ever brick a board. W3's escalation 6 recommends the rewrite and names the line, but no step id owns the edit, no acceptance criterion covers it, and W7-15 (store copy) is left to infer the correct positioning on its own. The brand's own definition of the game is wrong and unowned.

Following from that: no step decides what the game IS. If it is a visual-search / attention task, then legibility, density and silhouette novelty are the core loop — which makes W3-04/05/06/08 and W5-05/06 the product and most of W2 and W4 accessory. The plan has already implicitly accepted the redefinition (W3-02's probe measures scan cost, `(n+1)/(k+1)`, not planning cost) without ever writing it down, so every downstream workstream is optimising against an unstated premise.

No sound design work anywhere. DESIGN.md specifies audio behaviour and the working tree is mid-change on it (eight new pop*.wav, whoosh.wav deleted, generate-sfx.js and both native feedback modules modified — uncommitted). W2 is titled 'the reward loop (motion and feel)' and mentions audio only as a byproduct of W2-08's combo. Feel is half sound; the plan has twelve steps of pixels and zero of audio, on top of an unfinished audio change nobody is reviewing.

No step counts the words. W1-06's own text concedes 'the copy is the one place this workstream adds text to a game that has almost none'. Across the plan: 'No ad available right now — Retry is free' and 'Hint unavailable' (W0-04), three tutorial lines (W1-06), 'Perfect!' (W2-06), "Today's board · done" and 'N-day streak · 1 saved' (W4-05/06), gallery labels and 'N of 26' (W4-07), share-card header (W4-08), notification copy (W4-09), Settings rows (W7-04), store screenshot captions (W5-14). A minimal game acquires a vocabulary by accretion and no one is holding the total.

No step reconciles the five save migrations into one. Named above under sequencing, but it is also missing work, not just mis-ordering: someone has to write the final 19-key array, the single schema-version key, and the single updated assertion at storage.test.ts:36, before five workstreams each write their own.

No step defines the exit criteria for the plan itself. There are eight workstreams and roughly 100 steps against a solo owner, one loaded Mac, one API 31 emulator, no physical device on any platform, and an iOS renderer that has not compiled since 2026-09-01. Nothing says which workstreams must land before the next Play release, or what evidence would justify starting W8 at all. W8's own escalation argues for deferral and then specifies fourteen steps anyway.
strongest_case_the_plan_is_wrong:
This is an exhaustive defect list wearing the costume of a product plan, and the defect that matters most is the one it found and then walked past. Its own measurement says the game's stated mechanic does not exist: removing an arrow only empties cells, so canExit is monotone, so no order can brick a board, so 50 random-greedy playthroughs cleared in exactly arrowCount taps. There is no puzzle. What ships is a visual-search task — and the plan never writes that down, never fixes PRODUCT.md, and never re-derives anything from it. Instead all eight workstreams optimise their own axis against the unexamined assumption that the current product is worth multiplying: W2 spends twelve steps making the feel of an undecided game feel better; W4 spends ten building retention machinery (daily, streak, push, store prompt) around a loop nobody has established is worth returning to, with no instrumentation to find out because W6 comes later; W8 specifies fourteen steps for a second platform whose own escalation argues for deferral. Meanwhile the three things a visual-search game actually lives on — a difficulty curve that moves, silhouettes that stay novel, and a board you can read — sit in W3 and in two steps of W5, behind all of it.

And the accumulation is invisible by construction. Every step carries a FLAGCHECK and a brand gate, and every one passes, because each is judged alone: one quiet ink-dim row, one small badge, one 20 dp glyph, one transient line. Nobody sums them. Add them up and the menu roughly doubles, chrome moves inside the board viewport that both documents fence off, and a game with almost no words acquires a dozen strings. The per-step brand gate is the plan's most-repeated ritual and its least effective one — it can only ever catch a single step going loud, never the composite going busy, which is the failure mode this brand actually has.

Against my own verdict, the strongest case: W0 is genuinely excellent, and it does not need a product thesis to justify it. W0-03 is the best step in the plan — it proves the reduce-motion collapse by computing blockerOpacityAt(1) = 0, states exactly what the non-animated fallback renders, and closes on a device recording with the OS flag set, not a unit test. W2-05's derivation of the terminal delays from BLOCKER_FLASH_MS, W1-07's refusal to invent the stall threshold, W3-04's τ fitted to two measurable endpoints, W7-11's refusal to name a cooldown — that is real discipline, better than most plans get. Fixing a fake TEST AD panel in a shipping build does not require knowing what the game is.

That case wins for W0 and I drop the objection there. It does not survive contact with W2, W4 and W8, which are where the money is: those workstreams cost the overwhelming majority of the effort, and every one of them is an answer to a question the plan never asked out loud.
